clue.text: Senior churchman aims to make news, literally

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior prelate of the Roman Catholic Church
aims or directs means points

explanation.surface: A top cleric sets out to get himself in the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news, literally' means the letters N, E, W, S taken one by one: north, east, west and south.
explanation.definitionFit: The four compass directions abbreviate to N, E, W and S, which spell out the word in the clue.

clue.text: Girls in play lock in the masters

indicators.note: the lock of hair is placed inside the word for the masters

parts.note: aces are experts or masters of a skill
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls in a drama are shut up with the schoolmasters.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who perform roles on stage are girls in a play.

clue.text: Little girl keeps too warm in simple Indian dress

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Di is a short form of the name Diana
hot means too warm

explanation.surface: A small girl stays cool in a plain Indian garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth worn by Hindu men in India is a plain traditional garment.

clue.text: Baby's discomfort comes from any sharp pressure

indicators.note: the answer emerges from the letters of the following words, rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An infant's soreness arises from any acute pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore skin irritation caused by wet diapers is an infant's common complaint.

clue.text: Bush in bloom almost covers half-acre

indicators.note: the last letter of the flower name is dropped

parts.note: a lily is a flower or bloom

indicators.note: the first two of the four letters of acre are taken

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub nearly fills a small plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub with fragrant purple or white flowers is a garden bush.

clue.text: What belongs to us little people, not anyone else

parts.note: ours means what belongs to us
elves are the little people of folklore

explanation.surface: A possessive group insists its property is for its own small folk only.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun for 'we' stresses that it is us and nobody besides.

clue.text: They're essential if Kelly's to take English

indicators.note: the outlaw's possessive name takes in the extra letter

parts.note: Ned Kelly was the Australian bushranger, so Kelly's gives Ned's

explanation.surface: Something is indispensable if an outlaw is to take on an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly is the famous Australian outlaw; his first name with the possessive S takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are things one cannot do without.

clue.text: Mocking remark by Goldwyn about new cars

indicators.note: the producer's first name is placed around the other piece

parts.note: Sam Goldwyn was the Hollywood film producer

indicators.note: new signals the letters of cars are made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A film mogul makes a snide comment about the latest automobiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting irony used to taunt someone is a scornful jibe.

clue.text: Many go and split up

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so many
leave means go away

explanation.surface: A lot of people depart and break up.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something by chopping it apart, as with a butcher's knife.

clue.text: Fortune to come from numbers game

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or fortune

explanation.surface: Wealth is to be won from a lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance where drawn numbers are matched, like bingo or a lottery.

clue.text: Finally trap strange arboreal mammal

indicators.note: the last letter of trap is taken
strange signals the letters of arboreal are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: In the end, ensnare an odd tree-dwelling beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The large white Arctic bear is a mammal.

clue.text: It provides comfort and peace around certain quarters

indicators.note: the word for peace goes around the compass letters

parts.note: amity means friendly peace
E and N are compass quarters, east and north

explanation.surface: Something gives ease and calm in some districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility that makes life pleasanter is a convenience.

clue.text: Rachel's eager to hold a winning club

indicators.note: the words Rachel's eager hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A woman is keen to hang on to a victorious team.
explanation.definitionFit: A London football club with many trophies to its name.

clue.text: Follow directions before use, stupid!

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north

indicators.note: stupid signals the letters of use are muddled

explanation.surface: Read the instructions before use, you fool!
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result is to result or succeed.

clue.text: Inspectors turn up to dismiss hard workers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to axe someone is to dismiss them
miners toil at the coalface, hard workers

explanation.surface: Officials come round to sack industrious labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who test or scrutinise candidates or work are assessors.

clue.text: Remedy wanted after head-on clash with Gorgons?

definitions.text: Remedy wanted after head-on clash with Gorgons?

parts.words: Remedy wanted after head-on clash with Gorgons?
parts.note: Gorgons have snakes for hair, so butting heads with one would mean snakebites needing a cure for poison

explanation.surface: After colliding with the snake-haired monsters, a cure is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A serum that counteracts snake poison is the remedy after bites.

clue.text: Kind of torture also cut short in article

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: the shortened cut goes inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for cut is removed

parts.note: to hack is to cut

explanation.surface: A form of torment is also abbreviated within a written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims HACK to HAC, which goes 'in' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A throbbing pain in a molar feels like a form of torment.

clue.text: Moment NCO0 gets rattled gives evasive answer

indicators.note: rattled signals the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A flustered corporal stonewalls when questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal to say anything is a dodge of the question.

clue.text: It is a chop cooked with a sweet flavour

indicators.note: cooked signals the letters are stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cut of meat prepared with a sugary taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A green nut used to flavour ice cream and desserts.

clue.text: Medication put on burns, initially, with oxygen

parts.note: to place is to put

indicators.note: the first letter of burns is taken

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Medicine is applied to burns at first, with oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given as if it were a real drug.

clue.text: Reportedly a way of increasing numbers in splinter groups

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word heard is spoken, not written

parts.note: procreation through sex is how populations grow

explanation.surface: Breakaway factions are said to be growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Factions that break away from a larger religious body.

clue.text: Upper House holds view that gets Brown upset

indicators.note: the word for view holds the other piece inside

parts.note: to see is to view

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: The upper chamber takes a stance that angers a man called Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works as a turnaround because this is a down clue, so the colour reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper chamber of a legislature, as in the US or ancient Rome.

clue.text: Insulting Lincoln got us four imprisoned

indicators.note: the president's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname
taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Rude President Lincoln jailed four of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and offensive in language.

clue.text: Marry one's sweetheart

parts.note: a unit is one
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Wed one's beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in wedlock is to bring together.

clue.text: More like one of the crowd

explanation.surface: Something more like a member of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional; also a film bit-part player in a background crowd scene.

clue.text: Derrick's game

explanation.definitionFit: Derrick was a 17th-century executioner whose name became a word for a gallows; also a word-guessing pencil game.

clue.text: Suitable place in hospital in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: the pleasant word surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A good spot in a hospital in agreeable surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable or apt position, as in finding one's place in life.

clue.text: Caesar, for instance, ordered tipple with ice

indicators.note: ordered signals the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The Roman general asked for a drink on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Julius Caesar is said to have had the falling sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar reportedly suffered seizures, a person with this condition.

clue.text: Cold? It's certainly not, fool!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
heat is the opposite of cold, so it is certainly not cold

explanation.surface: Is it cold? Not at all, you idiot!
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to deceive or swindle them.

clue.text: Past financial records reveal exaggerations

parts.note: over means finished or past
bank statements are financial records

explanation.surface: Old accounts expose overblown claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Claims that go beyond the truth are hyperboles.
